items.stem: You have a big idea for a community garden. Which action is small enough to finish this week?

options.label: Sketch one garden bed layout on paper
Build the entire garden this month
Wait until you have funding and tools

items.hint_text: Pick the option you could finish in one sitting.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. A single paper sketch is one sitting of work and gives you something to react to.
items.feedback_wrong: Building the whole garden or waiting for perfect tools are both too large for one week. A first step should be small enough to finish soon so you actually start.

items.stem: Which of these count as a good first step for a new project? Select all that apply.

options.label: Finish one small task this week
Design the final version completely
Write down the single next action
Launch to all users at once

items.hint_text: A first step is doable now, not the finished product.
items.feedback_correct: Right. One small task plus a written next action are both first steps you can finish this week.
items.feedback_wrong: A good first step is small and doable this week. Designing the final version or launching to everyone is the whole project, not a first step.

items.stem: Why does the module say that progress you can see matters?

options.label: Visible progress makes it easier to keep going
It proves the project is finished
It replaces the need for a plan

items.feedback_correct: Correct. Seeing progress supports momentum and gives you something to build on.
items.feedback_wrong: Seeing progress supports momentum and adjustment, not completion. A visible step is not the finished project, and it still needs a plan around it.

items.stem: Which actions help you notice progress and adjust? Select all that apply.

options.label: Mark off what you finished this week
Compare the result to your first step
Ignore results until the very end
Decide one change for next week

items.hint_text: Progress means reviewing what happened, not ignoring it.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. Reviewing what you finished, comparing it, and choosing a change all help you adjust.
items.feedback_wrong: Noticing progress means reviewing what you finished and adjusting from it. Waiting until the end hides problems and leaves no chance to change course.

items.stem: A teammate suggests adding three features before the first demo. What is the better scoping move?

options.label: Pick one feature to finish first
Build all three at once
Drop the demo entirely

items.hint_text: Which choice keeps the step finishable this week?
items.feedback_correct: Right. Choosing one feature keeps the step small and finishable this week.
items.feedback_wrong: Trying to build all three at once spreads effort and delays any result. Choosing one feature to finish first keeps the step small and done this week.

items.stem: Which statement best describes a good first step?

options.label: Small enough to finish this week
Big enough to impress everyone
Perfect before anyone sees it

items.hint_text: Judge the step by when you can finish it.
items.feedback_correct: Correct. A first step is judged by whether you can finish it soon.
items.feedback_wrong: A first step is judged by whether you can finish it soon, not by how impressive or perfect it looks. Big or flawless steps usually never get started.

items.stem: You want to start a study group. Which action is a first step rather than the whole project?

options.label: Ask two classmates to meet once this week
Run a study group for the whole semester
Write the full rules for every session

items.hint_text: Which action fits into a single week?
items.feedback_correct: Yes. One meeting with two people is something you can do this week.
items.feedback_wrong: One meeting with two people is something you can do this week. Running a semester-long group or writing every rule is the whole project, not a first step.

items.stem: Which of these are first steps you could finish this week? Select all that apply.

options.label: Draft one paragraph of the proposal
Interview one potential user
Finish the entire finished product
Complete the whole budget forecast

items.hint_text: A first step is a small piece, not the finished whole.
items.feedback_correct: Right. One paragraph and one interview are both finishable this week.
items.feedback_wrong: A first step is small and finishable this week. A complete product or a full budget forecast is the whole project, not the first move.

items.stem: You finished only part of your first step. What does the module suggest?

options.label: Look at what you did and adjust the next step
Abandon the idea completely
Pretend the step is complete

items.feedback_correct: Correct. Partial progress is still progress you can review and use.
items.feedback_wrong: Partial progress is still progress you can review and use. Quitting or pretending hides the information you need to adjust the next step.

items.stem: Why look back at a finished step before choosing the next one?

options.label: It shows what worked and what to change
It adds more tasks to the list
It proves the goal is reached

items.hint_text: Looking back is about learning, not finishing.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. Looking back tells you what worked so you can steer the next step.
items.feedback_wrong: Looking back is about learning from the result to steer the next step. It does not add tasks or prove the goal is finished.
